To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

wheat bran, wheat milling by-products, wheat milling fractions and wheat milling by-products fractions are not the same and that their composition, and thus their impact on bread quality and health benefits, is strongly dependent on the milling procedure and the type of wheat used.
the milling by-products of wheat flour production have different properties and impact on bread making.

the properties of wheat milling by-products are not only related to their origin but also to the degree of endosperm contamination and that the properties of fine weatings and of low grade flour are intrinsically more negative for bread making than those from coarse bran and weat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a sustainable and cost effective use for wheat milling by-products in bread production.
the development of a new bread making process in which the use of wheat by-products is increased.
the impact of wheat by-products, in particular their DF content on bread quality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the properties of wheat milling by-products are not related to their impact on bread quality.
the properties of wheat milling by-products are not only related to their origin in the milling process but also depend on the milling process and the wheat cultivar.
the more coarse the wheat milling by-products, the more favorable for bread making.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
coarse bran, coarse and fine weating are suitable for bread making.

the use of wheat milling by-products in bread making should be restricted to the coarsest by-products, as these are the most abundant and contain the lowest amounts of starch and lipophilic components.
coarse bran and weating are more suitable than fine weating and low grade flour for bread making.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the properties of wheat milling by-products are not only related to their endosperm contamination but are influenced by their composition and structure.

the impact of wheat by-products on bread making is highly dependent on the specific properties of the by-products and that the use of coarse bran and coarse weatings is not necessarily detrimental to bread making.
DF content and particle size, and to a lesser extent ash, are the most relevant properties of wheat by-products to predict their impact on bread quality.
